sanskrit: tasya bhṛtyā viguṇatāṃ yānti sarve kulodgatāḥ na ca bhṛtyaphalair arthaiḥ sa rājā saṃprayujyate
english: His servants, all of good lineage, fall away into worthlessness, and that king is never blessed with the fruits that loyal servants bring.

sanskrit: etān me saṃśayasthasya rājadharmān sudurlabhān bṛhaspatisamo buddhyā bhavāñ śaṃsitum arhati
english: To me, who stand in doubt, you—the equal of Bṛhaspati in wisdom—ought to expound these duties of a king, hard indeed to grasp.

sanskrit: śaṃsitā puruṣavyāghra tvaṃ naḥ kulahite rataḥ kṣattā caiva paṭuprajño yo naḥ śaṃsati sarvadā
english: You are our expounder, O tiger among men, devoted to the welfare of our line; and so too is the keen-witted Kṣattṛ (Vidura), who counsels us always.

sanskrit: tvattaḥ kulahitaṃ vākyaṃ śrutvā rājyahitodayam amṛtasyāvyayasyeva tṛptaḥ svapsyāmy ahaṃ sukham
english: Having heard from you the word that serves our house and brings forth the welfare of the realm, I shall sleep content and at ease, as though sated with imperishable nectar.

sanskrit: kīdṛṣāḥ saṃnikarṣasthā bhṛtyāḥ syur vā guṇānvitāḥ kīdṛśaiḥ kiṃkulīnair vā saha yātrā vidhīyate
english: What manner of servants, endowed with virtues, should stand close at hand? With men of what character and what lineage should one's course of governance be conducted?

sanskrit: na hy eko bhṛtyarahito rājā bhavati rakṣitā rājyaṃ cedaṃ janaḥ sarvas tat kulīno 'bhiśaṃsati
english: For no king, bereft of servants, can be a protector all alone; and as for this realm, all people of good birth proclaim it so.

sanskrit: na hi praśāstuṃ rājyaṃ hi śakyam ekena bhārata asahāyavatā tāta naivārthāḥ ke cid apy uta labdhuṃ labdhvā cāpi sadā rakṣituṃ bharatarṣabha
english: For a kingdom cannot be governed by one alone, O Bhārata; without helpers, dear son, no aims whatsoever can be won—nor, once won, ever kept secure, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yasya bhṛtyajanaḥ sarvo jñānavijñānakovidaḥ hitaiṣī kulajaḥ snigdhaḥ sa rājyaphalam aśnute
english: Bhīṣma said: He whose every servant is skilled in knowledge and discernment, well-wishing, of good birth, and affectionate—he enjoys the fruit of kingship.

sanskrit: mantriṇo yasya kulajā asaṃhāryāḥ sahoṣitāḥ nṛpater matidāḥ santi saṃbandhajñānakovidāḥ
english: He whose counsellors are well-born, incorruptible, long resident at his side, givers of sound counsel to the king, and versed in the knowledge of connections—

sanskrit: anāgatavidhātāraḥ kālajñānaviśāradāḥ atikrāntam aśocantaḥ sa rājyaphalam aśnute
english: who make provision for what has not yet come, are expert in the knowledge of timing, and grieve not for what is past—he enjoys the fruit of kingship.

sanskrit: samaduḥkhasukhā yasya sahāyāḥ satyakāriṇaḥ arthacintāparā yasya sa rājyaphalam aśnute
english: He whose helpers share alike in his sorrow and his joy, who act in truth and are bent on the care of his interests—he enjoys the fruit of kingship.

sanskrit: yasya nārto janapadaḥ saṃnikarṣagataḥ sadā akṣudraḥ satpathālambī sa rājyaphalabhāg bhavet
english: He whose countryfolk, ever near at hand, are free from distress, not mean of spirit, and steadfast upon the path of the good—he comes to partake of the fruit of kingship.

sanskrit: kośākṣapaṭalaṃ yasya kośavṛddhikarair janaiḥ āptais tuṣṭaiś ca satataṃ dhāryate sa nṛpottamaḥ
english: That king is best whose treasury and revenue-records are kept always by men who swell the treasury—men trusted and content.

sanskrit: koṣṭhāgāram asaṃhāryair āptaiḥ saṃcayatatparaiḥ pātrabhūtair alubdhaiś ca pālyamānaṃ guṇībhavet
english: His granary, when guarded by the incorruptible and the trusted, men intent on storing up, worthy of their trust and free from greed, becomes a source of strength.

sanskrit: vyavahāraś ca nagare yasya karmaphalodayaḥ dṛśyate śaṅkhalikhitaḥ sa dharmaphalabhāg bhavet
english: He in whose city the conduct of affairs is seen to bear the fruit of action, recorded clean as if by Śaṅkha and Likhita—he comes to partake of the fruit of righteousness.

sanskrit: saṃgṛhītamanuṣyaś ca yo rājā rājadharmavit ṣaḍvargaṃ pratigṛhṇan sa dharmāt phalam upāśnute
english: And the king who has won his men to himself, who knows the duties of a king and lays hold upon the sixfold body of policy—he gains the fruit that springs from dharma.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam nidarśanakaraṃ loke sajjanācaritaṃ sadā
english: Bhīṣma said: On this matter too they recount an ancient tale, ever instructive in the world and walked by the path of the good.

sanskrit: asyaivārthasya sadṛśaṃ yac chrutaṃ me tapovane jāmadagnyasya rāmasya yad uktam ṛṣisattamaiḥ
english: It is fitting to this very theme—what I heard in a penance-grove, told to Rāma the son of Jamadagni by the best of the sages.

sanskrit: vane mahati kasmiṃś cid amanuṣyaniṣevite ṛṣir mūlaphalāhāro niyato niyatendriyaḥ
english: In a certain great forest, untrodden by men, there dwelt a sage who lived on roots and fruits, self-restrained and master of his senses.

sanskrit: dīkṣādamaparaḥ śāntaḥ svādhyāyaparamaḥ śuciḥ upavāsaviśuddhātmā satataṃ satpathe sthitaḥ
english: Devoted to consecration and self-discipline, serene, supreme in private study of the Veda, pure, his soul cleansed by fasting, he stood always upon the path of the good.

sanskrit: tasya saṃdṛśya sadbhāvam upaviṣṭasya dhīmataḥ sarvasattvāḥ samīpasthā bhavanti vanacāriṇaḥ
english: Beholding the goodness of that wise one as he sat there, all the creatures who roamed the forest would gather close about him.

sanskrit: siṃhavyāghrāḥ saśarabhā mattāś caiva mahāgajāḥ dvīpinaḥ khaḍgabhallūkā ye cānye bhīmadarśanāḥ
english: Lions and tigers, śarabhas, and great rutting elephants, leopards, rhinoceroses, and bears, and others dreadful to look upon—

sanskrit: te sukhapraśnadāḥ sarve bhavanti kṣatajāśanāḥ tasyarṣeḥ śiṣyavac caiva nyagbhūtāḥ priyakāriṇaḥ
english: all these blood-eating beasts would come, asking after his welfare, lowly as disciples before that sage and eager to do him pleasure.

sanskrit: dattvā ca te sukhapraśnaṃ sarve yānti yathāgatam grāmyas tv ekaḥ paśus tatra nājahāc chvā mahāmunim
english: Having paid their respects, they would all depart as they had come; but one tame beast, a dog, would never leave the great sage.

sanskrit: bhakto 'nuraktaḥ satatam upavāsakṛśo 'balaḥ phalamūlotkarāhāraḥ śāntaḥ śiṣṭākṛtir yathā
english: Devoted, ever attached to him, gaunt and feeble from fasting, feeding on heaps of fruit and root, serene, and gentle as a cultured being in form.

sanskrit: tasyarṣer upaviṣṭasya pādamūle mahāmuneḥ manuṣyavad gato bhāvaḥ snehabaddho 'bhavad bhṛśam
english: Seated at the feet of that great sage, the dog's nature had grown well-nigh human, and it was bound to him by a deep and tender love.

sanskrit: tato 'bhyayān mahāvīryo dvīpī kṣatajabhojanaḥ śvārtham atyantasaṃduṣṭaḥ krūraḥ kāla ivāntakaḥ
english: Then there came on a leopard of mighty strength, a blood-eater, bent upon the dog—utterly savage, cruel, like Death the ender of all.

sanskrit: lelihyamānas tṛṣitaḥ pucchāsphoṭanatatparaḥ vyāditāsyaḥ kṣudhābhagnaḥ prārthayānas tadāmiṣam
english: Licking its lips, athirst, busily lashing its tail, its jaws agape, broken with hunger, it craved that flesh for its prey.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā krūram āyāntaṃ jīvitārthī narādhipa provāca śvā muniṃ tatra yat tac chṛṇu mahāmate
english: Seeing that fierce beast advancing, O lord of men, the dog, desiring life, spoke to the sage there—hear now what it said, O sagacious one.

sanskrit: śvaśatrur bhagavann atra dvīpī māṃ hantum icchati tvatprasādād bhayaṃ na syāt tasmān mama mahāmune
english: "Blessed one, here is the leopard, the foe of dogs, and it means to slay me; by your grace let there be no fear of it for me, O great sage."

sanskrit: munir uvāca na bhayaṃ dvīpinaḥ kāryaṃ mṛtyutas te kathaṃ cana eṣa śvarūparahito dvīpī bhavasi putraka
english: The sage said: "No fear of the leopard need you have, nor of death in any wise. Cast off the form of a dog—you become a leopard, my child."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataḥ śvā dvīpitāṃ nīto jāmbūnadanibhākṛtiḥ citrāṅgo visphuran hṛṣṭo vane vasati nirbhayaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the dog, turned into a leopard, his form bright as gold of Jambū, his limbs dappled, glistening and glad, dwelt in the forest without fear.

sanskrit: tato 'bhyayān mahāraudro vyāditāsyaḥ kṣudhānvitaḥ dvīpinaṃ lelihad vaktro vyāghro rudhiralālasaḥ
english: Then there came on a most fearsome tiger, its jaws agape, gripped by hunger, licking its mouth at the leopard, greedy for its blood.

sanskrit: vyāghraṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣudhābhagnaṃ daṃṣṭriṇaṃ vanagocaram dvīpī jīvitarakṣārtham ṛṣiṃ śaraṇam eyivān
english: Seeing the tiger, fanged and forest-ranging, broken with hunger, the leopard, to save its life, took refuge with the sage.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃvāsajaṃ sneham ṛṣiṇā kurvatā sadā sa dvīpī vyāghratāṃ nīto ripubhir balavattaraḥ tato dṛṣṭvā sa śārdūlo nābhyahaṃs taṃ viśāṃ pate
english: Then, by the sage who ever bore for him the love bred of long dwelling together, that leopard was turned into a tiger, mightier than his foes; and seeing this, the tiger that had come did not strike him down, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: sa tu śvā vyāghratāṃ prāpya balavān piśitāśanaḥ na mūlaphalabhogeṣu spṛhām apy akarot tadā
english: But the dog, having attained tigerhood, now strong and a flesh-eater, no longer felt any longing then for fare of roots and fruits.

sanskrit: yathā mṛgapatir nityaṃ prakāṅkṣati vanaukasaḥ tathaiva sa mahārāja vyāghraḥ samabhavat tadā
english: As the lord of beasts forever craves the dwellers of the wood, even so, great king, did that tiger then become.

sanskrit: vyāghras tūṭajamūlasthas tṛptaḥ supto hatair mṛgaiḥ nāgaś cāgāt tam uddeśaṃ matto megha ivotthitaḥ
english: The tiger, sated on the deer he had slain, lay sleeping at the foot of the hermit's hut; then to that spot came an elephant in rut, risen like a thundercloud.

sanskrit: prabhinnakaraṭaḥ prāṃśuḥ padmī vitatamastakaḥ suviṣāṇo mahākāyo meghagambhīranisvanaḥ
english: His temples streaming with rut, tall, marked with the lotus-sign, his head broad and high, finely tusked, vast of body, his cry deep as a thundercloud's.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā kuñjaraṃ mattam āyāntaṃ madagarvitam vyāghro hastibhayāt trastas tam ṛṣiṃ śaraṇaṃ yayau
english: Seeing that rutting elephant approach, proud in its frenzy, the tiger, terrified by fear of the elephant, went to the sage for refuge.

sanskrit: tato 'nayat kuñjaratāṃ taṃ vyāghram ṛṣisattamaḥ mahāmeghopamaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ sa bhīto 'bhavad gajaḥ
english: Then that best of sages led the tiger into elephanthood; and seeing him like a great cloud, the other elephant was filled with dread.

sanskrit: tataḥ kamalaṣaṇḍāni śallakīgahanāni ca vyacarat sa mudā yuktaḥ padmareṇuvibhūṣitaḥ
english: Then with joy he roamed among the lotus-beds and the dense śallakī thickets, adorned with the pollen of the lotuses.

sanskrit: kadā cid ramamāṇasya hastinaḥ sumukhaṃ tadā ṛṣes tasyoṭajasthasya kālo 'gacchan niśāniśam
english: And so, as the elephant disported himself in contentment, the days and nights of that sage who dwelt in his hut of leaves passed pleasantly by.

sanskrit: athājagāma taṃ deśaṃ kesarī kesarāruṇaḥ girikandarajo bhīmaḥ siṃho nāgakulāntakaḥ
english: Then there came to that place a lion, ruddy-maned, born of a mountain cavern, terrible, the destroyer of the elephant kind.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā siṃham āyāntaṃ nāgaḥ siṃhabhayākulaḥ ṛṣiṃ śaraṇam āpede vepamāno bhayāturaḥ
english: Seeing that lion advance, the elephant, distraught with fear of the lion, took refuge with the sage, trembling and stricken with dread.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa siṃhatāṃ nīto nāgendro muninā tadā vanyaṃ nāgaṇayat siṃhaṃ tulyajātisamanvayāt
english: Then that lordly elephant, turned into a lion by the sage, reckoned the wild lion as nothing, being now of like kind with it.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca so 'naśat siṃho vanyo bhīsannavāgbalaḥ sa cāśrame 'vasat siṃhas tasminn eva vane sukhī
english: And seeing him, the wild lion fled away, its voice and strength failing for fear; while the new-made lion dwelt happily at the hermitage in that same forest.

sanskrit: na tv anye kṣudrapaśavas tapovananivāsinaḥ vyadṛśyanta bhayatrastā jīvitākāṅkṣiṇaḥ sadā
english: But the other lesser beasts who dwelt in the penance-grove were no longer to be seen—forever cowering in fear and clinging to their lives.

sanskrit: kadā cit kālayogena sarvaprāṇivihiṃsakaḥ balavān kṣatajāhāro nānāsattvabhayaṃkaraḥ
english: At length, by the working of fate, there came one that did harm to all living things, mighty, a blood-eater, a terror to creatures of every kind—

sanskrit: aṣṭapād ūrdhvacaraṇaḥ śarabho vanagocaraḥ taṃ siṃhaṃ hantum āgacchan munes tasya niveśanam
english: a śarabha, eight-footed, walking with limbs upraised, a forest-ranger, came to the abode of that sage to slay the lion.

sanskrit: taṃ muniḥ śarabhaṃ cakre balotkaṭam ariṃdama tataḥ sa śarabho vanyo muneḥ śarabham agrataḥ dṛṣṭvā balinam atyugraṃ drutaṃ saṃprādravad bhayāt
english: That śarabha the sage made surpassing in strength, O subduer of foes; and then the wild śarabha, beholding before the sage a śarabha mighty and most fierce, fled swiftly away in fear.

sanskrit: sa evaṃ śarabhasthāne nyasto vai muninā tadā muneḥ pārśvagato nityaṃ śārabhyaṃ sukham āptavān
english: Thus set by the sage into the estate of a śarabha, he kept ever at the sage's side and enjoyed the happy condition of a śarabha.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarabhasaṃtrastāḥ sarve mṛgagaṇā vanāt diśaḥ saṃprādravan rājan bhayāj jīvitakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Then all the herds of deer, terrified by the śarabha, fled from the forest to every quarter, O king, in fear and clinging to their lives.

sanskrit: śarabho 'py atisaṃduṣṭo nityaṃ prāṇivadhe rataḥ phalamūlāśanaṃ śāntaṃ naicchat sa piśitāśanaḥ
english: And the śarabha, grown utterly savage, ever bent on the slaughter of living things, that flesh-eater no longer desired the peaceful fare of fruit and root.

sanskrit: tato rudhiratarṣeṇa balinā śarabho 'nvitaḥ iyeṣa taṃ muniṃ hantum akṛtajñaḥ śvayonijaḥ
english: Then the śarabha, seized by a mighty thirst for blood, sought to slay that very sage—ungrateful, born of the womb of a dog.

sanskrit: tatas tena tapaḥśaktyā vidito jñānacakṣuṣā vijñāya ca mahāprājño muniḥ śvānaṃ tam uktavān
english: Then, perceiving him by the power of his penance through the eye of knowledge, the sage of great wisdom, knowing all, spoke thus to that dog:

sanskrit: śvā tvaṃ dvīpitvam āpanno dvīpī vyāghratvam āgataḥ vyāghro nāgo madapaṭur nāgaḥ siṃhatvam āptavān
english: "A dog, you attained leopardhood; a leopard, you came to tigerhood; the tiger became an elephant fierce in rut, and the elephant attained lionhood;

sanskrit: siṃho 'tibalasaṃyukto bhūyaḥ śarabhatāṃ gataḥ mayā snehaparītena na vimṛṣṭaḥ kulānvayaḥ
english: the lion, endowed with surpassing strength, passed further into a śarabha. Overcome by affection, I gave no thought to the lineage of your stock."

sanskrit: yasmād evam apāpaṃ māṃ pāpa hiṃsitum icchasi tasmāt svayonim āpannaḥ śvaiva tvaṃ hi bhaviṣyasi
english: "Since thus, O wicked one, you wish to do harm to me who am sinless, therefore, returning to your own birth, a dog you shall once more become."

sanskrit: tato munijanadveṣād duṣṭātmā śvākṛto 'budhaḥ ṛṣiṇā śarabhaḥ śaptaḥ svaṃ rūpaṃ punar āptavān
english: Then, through hatred of the sage's person, the wicked-souled and foolish śarabha, cursed by the sage, took on once more his form of a dog.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sa śvā prakṛtim āpannaḥ paraṃ dainyam upāgamat ṛṣiṇā huṃkṛtaḥ pāpas tapovanabahiṣkṛtaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: That dog, restored to his own nature, fell into the depths of misery; rebuked with a "Begone!" by the sage, the wretch was cast out of the penance-grove.

sanskrit: evaṃ rājñā matimatā viditvā śīlaśaucatām ārjavaṃ prakṛtiṃ sattvaṃ kulaṃ vṛttaṃ śrutaṃ damam
english: Thus a wise king, having tested a man's good conduct and purity, his uprightness, disposition, and worth, his lineage, his behaviour, his learning and self-control,

sanskrit: anukrośaṃ balaṃ vīryaṃ bhāvaṃ saṃpraśamaṃ kṣamām bhṛtyā ye yatra yogyāḥ syus tatra sthāpyāḥ suśikṣitāḥ
english: his compassion, strength, valour, temper, calmness, and forbearance—should appoint such well-trained servants each to the office for which he is fit.

sanskrit: nāparīkṣya mahīpālaḥ prakartuṃ bhṛtyam arhati akulīnanarākīrṇo na rājā sukham edhate
english: A guardian of the earth ought not to appoint a servant without testing him; the king who is thronged with men of low birth does not prosper in ease.

sanskrit: kulajaḥ prakṛto rājñā tatkulīnatayā sadā na pāpe kurute buddhiṃ nindyamāno 'py anāgasi
english: A man of good birth, appointed by the king, by reason of that good birth never sets his mind on wickedness, even when reproached though he be guiltless.

sanskrit: akulīnas tu puruṣaḥ prakṛtaḥ sādhusaṃkṣayāt durlabhaiśvaryatāṃ prāpto ninditaḥ śatrutāṃ vrajet
english: But a man of low birth, appointed through the ruin of worthier folk, having gained a lordship hard for him to win, if reproached will turn to enmity.

sanskrit: kulīnaṃ śikṣitaṃ prājñaṃ jñānavijñānakovidam sarvaśāstrārthatattvajñaṃ sahiṣṇuṃ deśajaṃ tathā
english: One well-born, trained, and wise, skilled in knowledge and discernment, knowing the true sense of all the treatises, enduring, and native to the land;

sanskrit: kṛtajñaṃ balavantaṃ ca kṣāntaṃ dāntaṃ jitendriyam alubdhaṃ labdhasaṃtuṣṭaṃ svāmimitrabubhūṣakam
english: grateful and strong, patient, self-disciplined, master of his senses, free from greed, content with what he has, and eager for the good of his master's friends;

sanskrit: sacivaṃ deśakālajñaṃ sarvasaṃgrahaṇe ratam satkṛtaṃ yuktamanasaṃ hitaiṣiṇam atandritam
english: a minister who knows place and time, devoted to the gathering of all things needful, honoured, steady of mind, well-wishing, and never slothful;

sanskrit: yuktācāraṃ svaviṣaye saṃdhivigrahakovidam rājñas trivargavettāraṃ paurajānapadapriyam
english: of fitting conduct within his own domain, skilled in alliance and in war, knowing the threefold ends of the king, and beloved of townsfolk and countryfolk alike;

sanskrit: khātakavyūhatattvajñaṃ balaharṣaṇakovidam iṅgitākāratattvajñaṃ yātrāyānaviśāradam
english: versed in the truth of entrenchments and battle-arrays, skilled in heartening the troops, knowing the meaning of gesture and demeanour, and expert in the march and the campaign;

sanskrit: hastiśikṣāsu tattvajñam ahaṃkāravivarjitam pragalbhaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ dāntaṃ balinaṃ yuktakāriṇam
english: learned in the training of elephants, free of arrogance, bold, deft, self-controlled, strong, and acting fittingly;

sanskrit: cokṣaṃ cokṣajanākīrṇaṃ suveṣaṃ sukhadarśanam nāyakaṃ nītikuśalaṃ guṇaṣaṣṭyā samanvitam
english: pure, surrounded by pure folk, well-attired and pleasing to behold, a leader skilled in statecraft, endowed with the sixty virtues—

sanskrit: astabdhaṃ praśritaṃ śaktaṃ mṛduvādinam eva ca dhīraṃ ślakṣṇaṃ maharddhiṃ ca deśakālopapādakam
english: unstubborn, humble, capable, soft of speech, steadfast, gentle, of great means, and able to provide for place and occasion—

sanskrit: sacivaṃ yaḥ prakurute na cainam avamanyate tasya vistīryate rājyaṃ jyotsnā grahapater iva
english: the king who appoints such a minister and never slights him—his realm spreads wide as the moonlight of the lord of planets.

sanskrit: etair eva guṇair yukto rājā śāstraviśāradaḥ eṣṭavyo dharmaparamaḥ prajāpālanatatparaḥ
english: A king endowed with these very virtues, skilled in the treatises, supreme in dharma and intent on guarding his subjects, is one to be desired.

sanskrit: dhīro marṣī śuciḥ śīghraḥ kāle puruṣakāravit śuśrūṣuḥ śrutavāñ śrotā ūhāpohaviśāradaḥ
english: Steadfast, forbearing, pure, swift, knowing in due season the worth of manly effort; willing to learn, learned, a good listener, and skilled in weighing for and against;

sanskrit: medhāvī dhāraṇāyukto yathānyāyopapādakaḥ dāntaḥ sadā priyābhāṣī kṣamāvāṃś ca viparyaye
english: of keen intellect, sure of memory, doing all things as justice requires, self-controlled, ever speaking kindly, and forbearing in adversity;

sanskrit: dānācchede svayaṃkārī sudvāraḥ sukhadarśanaḥ ārtahastaprado nityam āptaṃmanyo naye rataḥ
english: deciding for himself in giving and withholding, easy of approach, pleasant to behold, ever stretching out a hand to the distressed, trusting and trusted, and devoted to right policy;

sanskrit: nāhaṃvādī na nirdvaṃdvo na yatkiṃcanakārakaḥ kṛte karmaṇy amoghānāṃ kartā bhṛtyajanapriyaḥ
english: not given to boasting of himself, not indifferent, not one to act at random, a doer of deeds that never fail once undertaken, and beloved of his servants.
